title: A common respiration step can give later oxygen decline midpoints in older North Pacific water under fixed transport
abstract: A North Pacific study used later oxygen decline midpoints in older water to reject a simultaneous increase in local respiration. We test that inference under stationary transport. A common uniform respiration step gives an exact deficit ramp with midpoint equal to the common start plus half the transit age. The published midpoint-AOU slope equals this response for a fitted baseline rate of 4.32 umol/kg/yr. This is a consistency calculation, not a rate measurement. For an age density g, the normalized respiration kernel is its survivor function divided by mean age. For exponential ages this equals g, so respiration and boundary-oxygen changes have identical normalized responses for any history. Respiration and ventilation-rate perturbations in a box are also equal at first order after amplitude scaling. Synthetic tests at the published ship sampling years show that a common respiration step can give later fitted midpoints in older water and that ramp limits can move those midpoints. Restricted annual shape fits have nearly equal errors for respiration and boundary inputs. The result limits causal inference from timing; it does not identify the actual cause or refute independent outcrop evidence. Uniform respiration, stationary transport and AOU proportional to age are explicit assumptions.

display.caption: A common respiration step gives later half-response times in older water. The published midpoint-AOU slope fits this idealized counterexample. Exponential transit ages give equal normalized boundary and respiration responses.
